treatment_plan.summary: 67-year-old female with non-valvular atrial fibrillation (CHA₂DS₂-VASc 4) on warfarin (INR 2.4), presenting with NSTEMI status-post primary PCI with drug-eluting stent, and concomitant Type 2 Diabetes. This complex dual-pathology case requires a tailored antithrombotic strategy balancing thrombotic risk (AF stroke risk + stent thrombosis) against bleeding risk on triple therapy. She is at high stroke risk and high bleeding risk given age >65 and triple antithrombotic combination.

recommendations.intervention: Short-term triple therapy: VKA (warfarin) with INR target 2.0–2.5 + Aspirin 75–100 mg daily + Clopidogrel 75 mg daily for 6 months post-ACS with DES
recommendations.rationale: This 67F with NSTEMI post-PCI with DES and AF (CHA₂DS₂-VASc 4) requires triple therapy in the initial period per NSTEMI/AF co-management guidance, given ACS setting with DES and moderate-to-high thrombo-embolic risk.

recommendations.intervention: Long-term therapy after triple therapy period: VKA (warfarin) with INR target 2.0–3.0 + Clopidogrel 75 mg daily (or alternatively Aspirin 75–100 mg daily) from 6 months up to 12 months post-PCI
recommendations.rationale: After the initial 6-month triple therapy period for this 67F with AF and post-DES for ACS, the regimen should be de-escalated to VKA plus a single antiplatelet agent (clopidogrel 75 mg daily preferred) to reduce bleeding risk while maintaining stroke prevention for her high CHA₂DS₂-VASc score.

recommendations.intervention: Lifelong VKA (warfarin) monotherapy with INR target 2.0–3.0 after completion of dual/triple therapy period (~12 months post-PCI), unless recurrent cardiovascular event
recommendations.rationale: This 67F with non-valvular AF (CHA₂DS₂-VASc 4) requires lifelong oral anticoagulation for stroke prevention. After completion of post-ACS antiplatelet therapy, VKA monotherapy is recommended, with concomitant antiplatelet therapy not prescribed absent a subsequent cardiovascular event.

recommendations.intervention: When VKA is given in combination with clopidogrel or low-dose aspirin, maintain INR range 2.0–2.5 (careful regulation of anticoagulation dose intensity)
recommendations.rationale: During triple therapy and VKA-plus-single-antiplatelet phases in this 67F, the INR should be maintained at the lower range of 2.0–2.5 to minimise bleeding risk associated with combination antithrombotic therapy. Her current INR of 2.4 is within this target range.

recommendations.intervention: NOAC-based antithrombotic strategy as alternative: Rivaroxaban 15 mg daily (or 10 mg if eGFR 30–50 mL/min) + Clopidogrel 75 mg daily (or ticagrelor 90 mg BD or prasugrel 10 mg once daily)
recommendations.rationale: This 67F with AF post-PCI with DES may benefit from NOAC-based dual pathway therapy, which has been shown to cause less bleeding than standard triple therapy (DAPT + warfarin) in AF patients undergoing PCI with DES. Requires discussion with patient and availability assessment.

recommendations.intervention: NOAC-based triple therapy alternative: Rivaroxaban 2.5 mg BD + DAPT (Aspirin 75–100 mg daily + Clopidogrel 75 mg once daily)
recommendations.rationale: An alternative lower-dose rivaroxaban triple therapy regimen for this 67F with AF and post-PCI DES. Duration of DAPT depends on stent thrombosis versus bleeding risk. Note: this dose of rivaroxaban is yet to be registered in Malaysia per the CPG.

recommendations.intervention: Statin therapy (high potency, e.g. Atorvastatin 80 mg daily or Simvastatin 40 mg daily) — for secondary CVD prevention and T2DM in patient aged >40 years
recommendations.rationale: This 67F with NSTEMI post-PCI requires high-dose statin therapy for secondary prevention. She also has T2DM and is aged >40 years, meeting criteria for statin therapy regardless of baseline LDL-C level.

recommendations.intervention: Metformin — preferred first-line therapy for Type 2 Diabetes in this patient
recommendations.rationale: This 67F has T2DM requiring glucose management. Metformin is the preferred first-line therapy per CPG guidance. Renal function should be checked before initiation; metformin should only be stopped if GFR <30 mL/min per 1.73 m².

recommendations.intervention: Unfractionated heparin or LMWH (e.g. Enoxaparin) — acute anticoagulation during NSTEMI management
recommendations.rationale: This 67F with NSTEMI post-PCI should have received acute anticoagulation with UFH or LMWH as part of standard in-hospital management. An uninterrupted strategy of OAC is preferred with radial access as first choice.

recommendations.intervention: Fondaparinux — alternative anticoagulant for UA/NSTEMI patients treated conservatively
recommendations.rationale: Alternative anticoagulant option for this 67F with NSTEMI. Best used in patients treated conservatively; if invasive strategy is planned, UFH should be given during PCI as fondaparinux is associated with catheter-related thrombus.

recommendations.intervention: ACE inhibitor (e.g. Ramipril) — early initiation for LV dysfunction, diabetes, and post-MI cardioprotection
recommendations.rationale: This 67F with NSTEMI and T2DM should receive an ACE inhibitor early for cardioprotection. ACE-I should be considered long-term to prevent recurrent ischemia in this patient with established CVD.

recommendations.intervention: Beta-blocker (e.g. Metoprolol 25 mg BD, target 100 mg BD, or Bisoprolol 1.25 mg OD, target 10 mg OD) — unless contraindicated
recommendations.rationale: This 67F post-NSTEMI requires early beta-blocker administration for anti-ischaemic benefit and should be continued indefinitely in the presence of LV dysfunction (LVEF <40%). Should be administered early if no contraindications.

recommendations.intervention: Radial access preferred as first choice for PCI even during therapeutic anticoagulation (INR 2–3)
recommendations.rationale: This 67F on warfarin undergoing PCI for NSTEMI should have radial access used as first choice to minimise bleeding risk, given she is an anticoagulated AF patient at very high risk of thrombo-embolism.

recommendations.intervention: Lipid profile (TC, LDL-C, HDL-C, TG) — baseline and ongoing cardiovascular risk assessment
recommendations.rationale: This 67F with NSTEMI, AF, and T2DM requires lipid assessment to guide statin therapy intensity and monitor LDL-C targets for very high-risk CVD management.

recommendations.intervention: HbA1c — baseline glycaemic assessment and ongoing monitoring for T2DM management
recommendations.rationale: This 67F with T2DM requires HbA1c monitoring. Target should be individualised; given her pre-existing CVD (post-NSTEMI), an intermediate initial target of 6.6–7.4% is recommended, with tightening to ≤6.5% if achievable without hypoglycaemia.

recommendations.intervention: INR monitoring — weekly initially, then at stable intervals; target INR 2.0–2.5 during combination antithrombotic therapy, 2.0–3.0 during warfarin monotherapy
recommendations.rationale: This 67F on warfarin requires regular INR monitoring. Current INR 2.4 is within the target range for combination therapy (2.0–2.5). When on VKA monotherapy, target shifts to 2.0–3.0 (target 2.5).

recommendations.intervention: Gastric protection with a proton pump inhibitor (PPI) — should be considered where necessary during triple antithrombotic therapy
recommendations.rationale: This 67F on triple antithrombotic therapy (VKA + aspirin + clopidogrel) is at increased risk of gastrointestinal bleeding. PPI co-prescription is recommended per the antithrombotic strategy table footnote.

recommendations.intervention: Assess bleeding risk using HAS-BLED score — score ≥3 indicates high risk requiring caution and regular review
recommendations.rationale: This 67F on triple antithrombotic therapy with age >65 (HAS-BLED component 'E') requires formal bleeding risk assessment. The HAS-BLED score should be calculated to guide intensity of antithrombotic strategy.

recommendations.intervention: Assess cardiovascular risk using Framingham Risk Score — for comprehensive CVD risk stratification in T2DM management
recommendations.rationale: This 67F with T2DM, NSTEMI, and AF requires comprehensive cardiovascular risk assessment using validated risk calculators to guide intensity of lipid-lowering and BP management.

monitoring.schedule: Weekly until stable, then at regular intervals; maintain INR 2.0–2.5 during combination antithrombotic therapy, INR 2.0–3.0 (target 2.5) during warfarin monotherapy
monitoring.target: INR 2.0–2.5 during combination therapy; INR 2.0–3.0 during VKA monotherapy

monitoring.schedule: Every 3 months initially, then every 3–6 months when stable
monitoring.target: 6.6–7.4% initially (given CVD); tighten to ≤6.5% if achievable without hypoglycaemia

monitoring.schedule: Baseline and 4–12 weeks after statin initiation, then annually
monitoring.target: <1.8 mmol/L (or ≥50% reduction from baseline) for very high-risk CVD

monitoring.schedule: Baseline and periodically; essential for dose adjustment of anticoagulants and metformin
monitoring.target: Monitoring for dose adjustment; metformin contraindicated if GFR <30 mL/min/1.73m²

monitoring.schedule: Acute setting: maintain <8 mmol/L; ongoing monitoring per T2DM management
monitoring.target: <8 mmol/L in acute setting; individualised targets post-discharge

monitoring.schedule: At initiation of antithrombotic therapy and at each follow-up
monitoring.target: HAS-BLED score assessment; score ≥3 indicates high risk requiring regular review

red_flags: Active or occult bleeding on triple antithrombotic therapy — reduce intensity of antiplatelet/anticoagulant regimen; seek urgent review
INR >3.5 — risk of intracranial haemorrhage increases exponentially; withhold warfarin and seek urgent haematology review
INR <2.0 during combination therapy — increased risk of ischaemic stroke and stent thrombosis; reassess anticoagulation and compliance
Recurrent ischaemic chest pain or acute stent thrombosis symptoms — urgent cardiology review and consider coronary angiography
Severe hypoglycaemia (requiring third-party assistance) — reassess glucose-lowering regimen, revise A1c target, and screen for CVD (associated with 9–20% CV event risk in next year)
Haemodynamic instability, ongoing myocardial ischaemia, or acute heart failure — immediate DCCV or intensive care management as appropriate
follow_up: 1–2 weeks post-discharge: reassess antithrombotic therapy tolerability, review INR trends, and confirm target INR 2.0–2.5 on combination therapy — if INR stable, extend monitoring interval
1 month: reassess symptom status, INR control, glycaemic control (HbA1c if not done pre-discharge), and renal function — if stable, continue current regimen
3 months: repeat HbA1c, lipid profile, renal function; reassess bleeding risk (HAS-BLED) and adjust antithrombotic intensity if needed
6 months: transition from triple therapy to VKA + single antiplatelet (clopidogrel 75 mg daily preferred) if no recurrent ischaemic events — reassess cardiovascular risk factors
12 months post-PCI: consider de-escalation to VKA monotherapy (INR 2.0–3.0) if no subsequent cardiovascular events — discontinue concomitant antiplatelet therapy

Ongoing: lifelong VKA monotherapy for AF stroke prevention (CHA₂DS₂-VASc 4); annual comprehensive cardiovascular and diabetic review including lipid profile, HbA1c, renal function, and bleeding risk assessment
Ongoing: statin therapy continued indefinitely for secondary CVD prevention and T2DM management

Ongoing: annual review of CPG currency — AF guideline published 2011; CVD risk guideline considers NOAC evidence; check for updated evidence on dual pathway antithrombotic strategies post-PCI in AF patients
unresolved_questions: The CPG AF §6.4.4 antithrombotic strategy (published 2011, 15 years old) predates the PIONEER AF-PCI, RE-DUAL PCI, and AUGUSTUS trials. Modern evidence favours NOAC-based dual pathway therapy over VKA-based triple therapy. A current guideline check is strongly warranted.

Specific P2Y12 inhibitor choice (clopidogrel vs ticagrelor vs prasugrel) for this 67F post-PCI not fully addressed — the AF CPG recommends clopidogrel 75 mg daily; the CVD risk CPG also lists ticagrelor and prasugrel as alternatives. Prasugrel should be avoided if age >75 or weight <60 kg (she is 67, so prasugrel may be considered after coronary angiography).

LV ejection fraction not documented — this affects ACE-I/beta-blocker indication intensity, antithrombotic strategy, and glycaemic target selection. Echocardiography should be performed if not already done.

HAS-BLED score not calculated — patient age >65 contributes 1 point; other components (hypertension, renal/liver function, bleeding history, labile INRs, drug/alcohol) not documented. Formal scoring required to guide antithrombotic intensity.
Renal function (eGFR/CrCl) not documented — required for dose adjustment of LMWH, enoxaparin, fondaparinux, rivaroxaban, and metformin. Creatinine clearance should be calculated.

The CPG AF guideline is published in 2011 (15 years old). The CVD Risk §9.5.2.1 section references newer NOAC evidence and specific regimens for AF post-PCI with DES. Cross-referencing with the most current ESC/EAPCI 2020 or 2024 consensus documents on AF-PCI antithrombotic management is recommended.

Duration of DAPT in the rivaroxaban 2.5 mg BD + DAPT regimen depends on stent thrombosis versus bleeding risk — patient-specific stent characteristics (type, length, complexity) not documented to determine exact duration.

Insulin is preferred for hospitalised T2DM patients per CPG interaction flags. Current patient status (inpatient vs outpatient) and glycaemic control not specified to determine if insulin initiation is needed acutely.

recommendations.intervention: Beta-blocker (e.g. Metoprolol 25 mg BD, target 100 mg BD, or Bisoprolol 1.25 mg OD, target 10 mg OD) — unless contraindicated
recommendations.rationale: This 67F post-NSTEMI requires early beta-blocker administration for anti-ischaemic benefit and should be continued indefinitely in the presence of LV dysfunction (LVEF <40%). Should be administered early if no contraindications.

recommendations.intervention: Radial access preferred as first choice for PCI even during therapeutic anticoagulation (INR 2–3)
recommendations.rationale: This 67F on warfarin undergoing PCI for NSTEMI should have radial access used as first choice to minimise bleeding risk, given she is an anticoagulated AF patient at very high risk of thrombo-embolism.

recommendations.intervention: Lipid profile (TC, LDL-C, HDL-C, TG) — baseline and ongoing cardiovascular risk assessment
recommendations.rationale: This 67F with NSTEMI, AF, and T2DM requires lipid assessment to guide statin therapy intensity and monitor LDL-C targets for very high-risk CVD management.

recommendations.intervention: HbA1c — baseline glycaemic assessment and ongoing monitoring for T2DM management
recommendations.rationale: This 67F with T2DM requires HbA1c monitoring. Target should be individualised; given her pre-existing CVD (post-NSTEMI), an intermediate initial target of 6.6–7.4% is recommended, with tightening to ≤6.5% if achievable without hypoglycaemia.

recommendations.intervention: INR monitoring — weekly initially, then at stable intervals; target INR 2.0–2.5 during combination antithrombotic therapy, 2.0–3.0 during warfarin monotherapy
recommendations.rationale: This 67F on warfarin requires regular INR monitoring. Current INR 2.4 is within the target range for combination therapy (2.0–2.5). When on VKA monotherapy, target shifts to 2.0–3.0 (target 2.5).

recommendations.intervention: Gastric protection with a proton pump inhibitor (PPI) — should be considered where necessary during triple antithrombotic therapy
recommendations.rationale: This 67F on triple antithrombotic therapy (VKA + aspirin + clopidogrel) is at increased risk of gastrointestinal bleeding. PPI co-prescription is recommended per the antithrombotic strategy table footnote.

recommendations.intervention: Assess bleeding risk using HAS-BLED score — score ≥3 indicates high risk requiring caution and regular review
recommendations.rationale: This 67F on triple antithrombotic therapy with age >65 (HAS-BLED component 'E') requires formal bleeding risk assessment. The HAS-BLED score should be calculated to guide intensity of antithrombotic strategy.

recommendations.intervention: Assess cardiovascular risk using Framingham Risk Score — for comprehensive CVD risk stratification in T2DM management
recommendations.rationale: This 67F with T2DM, NSTEMI, and AF requires comprehensive cardiovascular risk assessment using validated risk calculators to guide intensity of lipid-lowering and BP management.

red_flags: Active or occult bleeding on triple antithrombotic therapy — reduce intensity of antiplatelet/anticoagulant regimen; seek urgent review
INR >3.5 — risk of intracranial haemorrhage increases exponentially; withhold warfarin and seek urgent haematology review
INR <2.0 during combination therapy — increased risk of ischaemic stroke and stent thrombosis; reassess anticoagulation and compliance
Recurrent ischaemic chest pain or acute stent thrombosis symptoms — urgent cardiology review and consider coronary angiography
Severe hypoglycaemia (requiring third-party assistance) — reassess glucose-lowering regimen, revise A1c target, and screen for CVD (associated with 9–20% CV event risk in next year)
Haemodynamic instability, ongoing myocardial ischaemia, or acute heart failure — immediate DCCV or intensive care management as appropriate
follow_up: 1–2 weeks post-discharge: reassess antithrombotic therapy tolerability, review INR trends, and confirm target INR 2.0–2.5 on combination therapy — if INR stable, extend monitoring interval
1 month: reassess symptom status, INR control, glycaemic control (HbA1c if not done pre-discharge), and renal function — if stable, continue current regimen
3 months: repeat HbA1c, lipid profile, renal function; reassess bleeding risk (HAS-BLED) and adjust antithrombotic intensity if needed
6 months: transition from triple therapy to VKA + single antiplatelet (clopidogrel 75 mg daily preferred) if no recurrent ischaemic events — reassess cardiovascular risk factors
12 months post-PCI: consider de-escalation to VKA monotherapy (INR 2.0–3.0) if no subsequent cardiovascular events — discontinue concomitant antiplatelet therapy

Ongoing: lifelong VKA monotherapy for AF stroke prevention (CHA₂DS₂-VASc 4); annual comprehensive cardiovascular and diabetic review including lipid profile, HbA1c, renal function, and bleeding risk assessment
Ongoing: statin therapy continued indefinitely for secondary CVD prevention and T2DM management

Ongoing: annual review of CPG currency — AF guideline published 2011; CVD risk guideline considers NOAC evidence; check for updated evidence on dual pathway antithrombotic strategies post-PCI in AF patients
unresolved_questions: The CPG AF §6.4.4 antithrombotic strategy (published 2011, 15 years old) predates the PIONEER AF-PCI, RE-DUAL PCI, and AUGUSTUS trials. Modern evidence favours NOAC-based dual pathway therapy over VKA-based triple therapy. A current guideline check is strongly warranted.

Specific P2Y12 inhibitor choice (clopidogrel vs ticagrelor vs prasugrel) for this 67F post-PCI not fully addressed — the AF CPG recommends clopidogrel 75 mg daily; the CVD risk CPG also lists ticagrelor and prasugrel as alternatives. Prasugrel should be avoided if age >75 or weight <60 kg (she is 67, so prasugrel may be considered after coronary angiography).

LV ejection fraction not documented — this affects ACE-I/beta-blocker indication intensity, antithrombotic strategy, and glycaemic target selection. Echocardiography should be performed if not already done.

HAS-BLED score not calculated — patient age >65 contributes 1 point; other components (hypertension, renal/liver function, bleeding history, labile INRs, drug/alcohol) not documented. Formal scoring required to guide antithrombotic intensity.
Renal function (eGFR/CrCl) not documented — required for dose adjustment of LMWH, enoxaparin, fondaparinux, rivaroxaban, and metformin. Creatinine clearance should be calculated.

The CPG AF guideline is published in 2011 (15 years old). The CVD Risk §9.5.2.1 section references newer NOAC evidence and specific regimens for AF post-PCI with DES. Cross-referencing with the most current ESC/EAPCI 2020 or 2024 consensus documents on AF-PCI antithrombotic management is recommended.

Duration of DAPT in the rivaroxaban 2.5 mg BD + DAPT regimen depends on stent thrombosis versus bleeding risk — patient-specific stent characteristics (type, length, complexity) not documented to determine exact duration.

Insulin is preferred for hospitalised T2DM patients per CPG interaction flags. Current patient status (inpatient vs outpatient) and glycaemic control not specified to determine if insulin initiation is needed acutely.
